correctness.rationale: Under the canonical product decomposition, trace vanishing is the conjunction of two field-valued trace equations. For every nonzero matrix over a finite field, the functional C -> tr(AC) is nonzero because a nonzero entry a_ij is detected by E_ji, so its kernel has codimension one. This gives the three support-dependent orthogonal-set sizes exactly. Deleting the zero vertex and, precisely in the self-orthogonal case, the vertex itself gives the two degrees per support. E_12 and E_11 realize both square-trace types for n>=2. The minimum degree, vertex count, and divisibility filter then algebraically recover qr, n^2, and the individual factor orders. The packaged replay independently verifies the trace-functional kernels and all reconstruction formulas for five field-order pairs, including F4.

originality.rationale: The 2024 full survey explicitly leaves the direct-product trace graph as Problem 1. It also reproduces the prior general vertex-degree formula and the prior isomorphism invariant recovering only total ring order and matrix size. The accepted claim does not relabel the known degree formula as new: it extracts the exact degree fingerprint for the two-field semisimple case and proves that it recovers both simple-factor orders, yielding an if-and-only-if graph-isomorphism classification within this family. value.rationale: The result gives a complete and natural first case of an explicit open direction in the 2024 survey: trace graphs of direct products. It does more than tabulate degrees. The graph reconstructs each simple finite-field factor, sharpening the previously quoted invariant that sees only total ring order. This is a structural rigidity statement for a standard semisimple family, with a short proof based on nondegenerate trace pairings and a graph-intrinsic degree fingerprint.
